# Ginés Sánchez

> History is shaped by how people learn, decide, and act together.

Ginés is building ways to understand those patterns, anticipate where they
lead, and change their course. Alteridad puts that work to use for clients
today; the larger aim is a science of how societies change.

## Start

Bring Ginés a decision that stalls, a problem that keeps returning, or an idea
no one has put to work. Uncover what holds it in place, change the way the work
gets done, and hold the result up to scrutiny.

The main introduction is visible on arrival. Start, Projects, Book, and About
open within the same page, one section at a time. The email link is in the header.

## Projects

Projects being developed through Alteridad: tools for buying decisions,
responsibility, and how teams learn and act. They are works in progress, built
to put facts, responsibilities, and consequences in plain view.

- [Chieftain](https://chieftain.ing/): culture. Finding where useful
  observations stop before they can change a decision, and who gets to act.
- [MicroManager](https://micromanager.app/): incentives and responsibility.
  Making work, responsibility, and rewards easier to see and discuss.
- [Replena](https://replena.ai/): demand, inventory, and purchasing. Helping
  teams decide what to buy and when using demand and stock.
- [Alteridad](https://www.alteridad.org/): the company behind the work.

## Book

[Culture Decides](https://ginesanchez.com/#book) is a book in progress about
how culture shapes what we notice and do, and how to see, question, and change
it in practice.

## About

Ginés trained as an anthropologist, working with Ngäbe communities in Panama
on language, knowledge, and different ways of living. Alongside research he
made art and films; today he builds software, writes, and keeps drawing.
He asks whose knowledge counts, who can change a decision, and who shares in
what they create. He wants to follow those questions from teams to societies.

## A small settlement

Behind the homepage text, twenty-four drawn creatures from Ginés's sketchbook
live in a small settlement that grows out of what they need, notice, tell one
another and build together: a crossing over the creek, a store, a lookout and
gardens, each built by at least two of them and each changing what the others
can do next. Knowledge travels by meeting and can go stale; well-used routes
are drawn in; exhausted creatures are replaced by newcomers who know nothing.
It is a drawing experiment, not a model of society. It runs at natural speed,
pauses when the tab is hidden, and opens as a still scene for reduced motion.
